cards.front: Increase in mass and in number of individuals are twin characteristics of which feature of living organisms?
True or false: growth, reproduction and the ability to sense the environment are features of living organisms.
Who is called the “Darwin of the 20th century”?
Taxonomic studies recognise similarities shared among organisms both ‘A’ and ‘B’.
What is the common method of multiplication in fungi, filamentous algae and the protonema of mosses?
Why is reproduction not a defining characteristic of living organisms?
cards.back: Many organisms cannot reproduce (for example mules and sterile worker bees).

cards.front: For unicellular organisms like bacteria, unicellular algae and *Amoeba*, ‘A’ is synonymous with ‘B’.
True or false: in the majority of higher animals and plants, growth and reproduction are mutually exclusive events.
True or false: properties of tissues are not present in the constituent cells but arise from interactions among them.
What is the sum total of all chemical reactions in a living body?
What is the most obvious and technically complicated feature of all living organisms?
A brain-dead patient has no self-consciousness and never returns to normal life. Living or non-living?
Early man could easily perceive the difference between ______ matter and living organisms.
The number and types of organisms present on earth is called?
How many species are known and described till now?
Each name in binomial nomenclature has two components: ‘A’ and ‘B’.
cards.back:
A: generic name
B: specific epithet

cards.front: Who gave the binomial naming system now used by biologists worldwide?
What is the full form of ICBN?
cards.note: It provides the agreed principles for naming plants.

cards.front: Biological names are generally in ‘A’ language and written in ‘B’.
When handwritten, both words of a biological name are ______ ; printed, they are in ______ , to indicate their Latin origin.
In a binomial, how are the first letters of the first and second word written, respectively?
Standardising names so one organism has the same name all over the world is called?
In *Mangifera indica*, what do *Mangifera* and *indica* represent?
Scientific names of (A) human, (B) potato, (C) leopard?
Match: Man, Housefly, Mango, Wheat with *Mangifera indica*, *Triticum aestivum*, *Homo sapiens*, *Musca domestica*.
cards.back:
Man: *Homo sapiens*
Housefly: *Musca domestica*
Mango: *Mangifera indica*
Wheat: *Triticum aestivum*

cards.front: Who used *Systema Naturae* as the title of his publication?
Who wrote “Théorie élémentaire de la botanique”?
The process of placing organisms into taxa on the basis of characteristics is called?
The word systematics comes from the Latin ‘systema’. What does it mean?
What are the three basics of taxonomy?
The earliest classifications were based on the ______ of various organisms.
What is a genus?
cards.back: A group of related species with more characters in common than with species of other genera.

cards.front: Felidae and *Felis* represent which taxonomic categories, respectively?
*Solanum*, *Petunia* and *Datura* belong to which family?
A group of individual organisms with fundamental morphological similarities is called?
Which group of related genera has fewer similarities than a genus or species?
Fishes, amphibians, reptiles, birds and mammals together form which higher category?
As we go from species up to kingdom, what happens to the number of common characters?
Kingdom ← Phylum ← B ← Order ← A ← Genus ← Species. Find A and B.
Find the odd one: Chordata, Carnivora, *Solanum*, Mammalia.
cards.note: It is a genus; the others are higher categories.

cards.front: Find the odd one by rank: Sapindales, Anacardiaceae, Poales.
cards.note: It is a family; the others are orders.

cards.front: *Triticum aestivum* → *Triticum* → A → Poales → B → Angiospermae. Identify A and B.
Why is it harder to determine relationships at higher categories?
cards.back: Common characters are fewer in higher taxa.

cards.front: ‘Animals’, ‘mammals’ and ‘dogs’ represent taxa at what levels?
Each step in the hierarchy of classification represents a ______ or ______ .
All the taxonomic categories together constitute the ______ .
What is the highest category to which animals of all phyla are assigned?
A species determined on the basis of morphological characters is called?
Ernst Mayr proposed which concept of species?
Which classification is done with computers and uses all observable characteristics?
Why are taxonomic studies of plants and animals useful?
cards.back: They help agriculture, forestry and industry, and show our bio-resources and their diversity.
